channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Elevate Strategic Partnership to New Level
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on August 29-30 for a state visit. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Modi held talks to deepen strategic partnership and multifaceted cooperation. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year, with joint ventures increasing sevenfold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses SCO Summit on Real Economy, Transport, and Anti-Crisis Agenda
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the SCO Heads of State Council meeting in Bishkek on August 31-September 1. Uzbekistan aims to leverage the summit, celebrating the SCO's 25th anniversary, to advance practical economic, transport, and anti-crisis initiatives, viewing it as a tool for Eurasian cooperation.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister's State Visit to Uzbekistan Concludes with Signed Agreements
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi concluded his state visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30. High-level talks focused on deepening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other sectors. Discussions also covered international politics and regional issues, resulting in a package of bilateral agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Tashkent fountain sets two world records; travel to Turkey increases
item.description: News digest includes: a fountain in New Tashkent setting two world records, increased travel from Uzbekistan to Turkey, and an agreement to reach $5 billion in trade with India by 2030. New mechanisms for settling overdue debt in foreign trade are introduced.

item.title: Uzbek President to attend SCO Summit in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek from August 31 to September 1 for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Heads of State Council meeting and an "SCO plus" format meeting. Discussions will focus on SCO cooperation, security, economy, and transport. The Bishkek Declaration will be adopted.

item.title: Tribute Paid to Lal Bahadur Shastri in Tashkent
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid flowers at the monument of Lal Bahadur Shastri in Tashkent during his state visit. Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov accompanied him. The memorial commemorates Shastri, who signed the Tashkent Declaration in 1966 and passed away shortly after in the city.

item.title: Putin and Pashinyan to Discuss Armenia's EU vs. EAEU Choice in Bishkek
item.description: Russian President Putin and Armenian Prime Minister Pashinyan will discuss Armenia's future integration course, potentially including a referendum, during their meeting in Bishkek on September 1. Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia respects Armenia's decision-making process regarding its alignment with the EU or EAEU.

item.title: Vietnamese Vice President Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for Working Visit
item.description: Vo Thi Anh Xuan, Vice President of Vietnam, arrived in Kyrgyzstan on August 30 for a working visit. She was met at Manas International Airport by Daniyar Aman-geldiev, First Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. She will attend the SCO Plus summit and the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Sees Historical Link in Xi Jinping's Visit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Arslan Koychiev noted a historical connection between Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit and the journey of Chinese monk Xuanzang 1,400 years ago. Koychiev highlighted Xi's stop at Bas-Boltök, a site also visited by Xuanzang, and referenced Xi's article on bilateral relations.

item.title: Ukraine's Defense Needs Additional $27 Billion, Negotiating with Partners
item.description: Ukraine's defense requires an additional $27 billion, according to Yevhenii Khmara. The Ukrainian Ministry of Defense is negotiating with partner countries to secure these funds. Several options are being considered to address this funding gap.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit, coming from Tashkent. He will attend the SCO Heads of State Council meeting, an 'SCO Plus' format meeting, and the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan currently chairs the SCO.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India leaders conclude talks, aiming for $5 billion trade by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi summarized their talks, highlighting strong bilateral ties and strategic partnership. They noted India's digital achievements and agreed to boost mutual trade from $1.3 billion to $5 billion by 2030, signing key agreements and investment project frameworks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Sadyr Japarov and China's Xi Jinping hold informal meeting in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and Chinese President Xi Jinping held an informal meeting in Bishkek with their wives. The leaders discussed cooperation issues and upcoming official events in a cordial atmosphere, according to the presidential press service.

item.title: Mongolian President arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Plus meeting and World Nomad Games
item.description: Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit to attend the SCO Plus meeting and the opening of the 6th World Nomad Games. He was welcomed at the airport and will participate as an observer in the SCO meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Import Halal-Certified Meat from India Following Agricultural Minister's Visit
item.description: Uzbekistan will import meat from India certified as halal, according to the Minister of Agriculture. Agreements were reached on the participation of Uzbek specialists in meat preparation and slaughter processes in India, ensuring international and halal certifications.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Sign Numerous Documents to Strengthen Bilateral Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have signed a substantial package of documents aimed at strengthening their partnership across trade, economy, investment, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. The signing ceremony took place in the presence of Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

item.title: Russia preparing for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities, says Defense Ministry
item.description: The Russian Defense Ministry stated that Russia is preparing for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities. The ministry described this measure as a response to Kyiv's ongoing attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and its fuel and energy complex.

item.title: New mechanism to be introduced for settlement of overdue debt on foreign trade operations
item.description: A new mechanism for settling overdue debt on foreign trade operations will be introduced. Entrepreneurs will be granted a one-time, universal state amnesty until January 1, 2027, to settle overdue receivables from exports using their own funds.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to attend SCO summit in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek on August 31-September 1 for the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and an "SCO Plus" format meeting. Discussions will focus on expanding cooperation within the SCO and addressing regional and international issues. Several documents are expected to be adopted.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to visit Bishkek for SCO summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will be in Bishkek for an official visit from August 31 to September 1. He will participate in the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and a "SCO Plus" format meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan selects J-10C fighter jets over French Rafale
item.description: Uzbekistan has chosen Chinese J-10C fighter jets, ending speculation about acquiring French Rafale aircraft. The decision was highlighted during a state event celebrating 35 years of independence. The article details the history and specifications of the J-10C, explaining why it is considered the optimal choice for Uzbekistan's air force modernization.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India leaders review outcomes of fruitful talks
item.description: Leaders of Uzbekistan and India reviewed the results of their recent negotiations. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev noted that these productive discussions were a clear expression of the sincere friendship, high regard, and mutual trust between the two states.

item.title: SCO media to broadcast Xi Jinping's favorite quotes program
item.description: Leading media outlets in SCO member states, including Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, will broadcast a multilingual version of China Media Corporation's program 'Xi Jinping's Favorite Winged Expressions.' The series features selected ancient Chinese literary quotes used by Xi Jinping, covering topics like economy, innovation, and environment.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India sign 12 cooperation documents
item.description: Uzbekistan and India signed 12 bilateral documents following talks between President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Agreements cover cultural exchanges, Ayurveda, higher education, environmental protection, archaeological research, economic dialogue, tourism, geology, archives, and regional partnerships.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan collaborate on transport links within SCO framework
item.description: China and Kyrgyzstan are actively developing transport infrastructure, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project and improved border crossings. Chinese President Xi Jinping highlighted these efforts as crucial for regional connectivity, prosperity, and stability within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).

item.title: Uzbekistan and India's Gujarat State Establish Partnership Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's Samarkand region and India's Gujarat state will establish partnership relations. Documents were signed to deepen cooperation in trade, investment, culture, education, ecology, archaeology, and tourism following high-level talks.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Awarded Order of Friendship
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi received the Order of Friendship in Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the award, stating it signifies the Uzbek people's high esteem for Modi's contributions to strengthening historical friendship between the two nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Collects Over 5 Trillion Soums in Customs Duties via UzIMEI System
item.description: Uzbekistan has collected over 5 trillion soums in customs duties through the UzIMEI system in seven years. Since 2019, more than 97.8 million IMEI codes have been registered. In its first year, the system automatically registered 47.6 million devices for free.

item.title: Child Rescued in Nepal; Kazakh Citizen Missing in Tibet
item.description: A six-year-old girl was rescued alive in Nepal after being trapped for nearly three days following catastrophic floods. Meanwhile, authorities confirmed one Kazakh citizen is missing in Tibet, likely one of three Kazakh tourists who crossed into China. Search operations continue.

item.title: Uzbekistan Awards Indian PM Narendra Modi the Order of Friendship
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded Uzbekistan's Order of High Friendship at the Kuksaroy residence. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the award for Modi's contributions to strengthening historical friendship between the two nations. Discussions also covered elevating bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Agree to Increase Trade Turnover to $5 Billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase their trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. During talks between Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, key issues of cooperation in trade, economy, investment, and humanitarian spheres were discussed. The parties aim to elevate relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Agree to Increase Mutual Trade to $5 Billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase their mutual trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. During talks between Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, bilateral relations were discussed with the aim of elevating them to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year.

item.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 734, with 2,498 missing
item.description: The death toll from floods in Nepal has risen to 734, with an additional 2,498 people reported missing. Among the missing, 589 are foreign nationals. The high number of casualties and bodies being washed hundreds of kilometers downstream are causing significant difficulties in identification.

item.title: Kazatomprom establishes specialized cabinet at Kazakh-British Technical University
item.description: Kazatomprom has opened a specialized cabinet at the Kazakh-British Technical University (KBTU) for students in the "Uranium Business" program. The facility is equipped with modern equipment and will host theoretical and practical classes, lectures, and meetings with industry experts to enhance practical skills.

item.title: Uzbekistan Citizens' Travel to Turkey Increased by 17.7% Year-on-Year
item.description: In January-July of this year, over 166,000 citizens of Uzbekistan traveled to Turkey. This figure represents a 17.7% increase compared to the same period last year, indicating a rise in travel between the two countries.

item.title: China-Nepal Border Landslide: 16 Dead, 546 Missing; Climate Change Cited
item.description: A landslide on the China-Nepal border has resulted in 16 deaths and 546 missing persons. Experts attribute the disaster to glacier instability caused by long-term climate warming. Chinese authorities have allocated over $30 million for rescue efforts, with over 2,000 rescuers on site. 261 foreign nationals are among the missing.

item.title: Fire at Bishkek's 'Madina' Market Localized Over 400 Square Meters
item.description: A fire at the 'Madina' market in Bishkek has been localized, affecting approximately 400 square meters. Emergency services are working to extinguish remaining hotspots in containers. The preliminary cause is suspected to be a short circuit.

item.title: All Bishkek Fire Trucks Deployed to Combat 'Madina' Market Blaze
item.description: All available fire trucks in Bishkek were deployed to fight a large fire at the 'Madina' market. The fire, which started in a container and spread to stalls, is believed to have been caused by a short circuit. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Dengue Fever Cases Surge 85% in Afghanistan, WHO Reports
item.description: The World Health Organization reports an 85% increase in dengue fever cases in Afghanistan. The surge, along with rises in coronavirus and other infectious diseases, is straining the country's healthcare system due to seasonal outbreaks and shortages of medicine and resources.

item.title: Afghanistan border crossing closures reduce Pakistan-Tajikistan trade by 70%
item.description: The closure of Afghanistan's border crossings has led to a nearly 70% reduction in trade between Pakistan and Tajikistan. Exports from Pakistan to Tajikistan fell by 61.3% to $11.9 million, while imports decreased by 82.8% to $3.3 million.
